events.title: Senegal's Youth Olympics makes Olympics in Africa 'logical'
events.description: The Youth Olympics are to be hosted in Africa for the first time ever. The edition in Senegal is also a chance to prove the continent can host a full Olympics in the future.

events.title: African leaders herald $16B Dangote oil refinery in Kenya
events.description: An oil refinery on Kenya's coast is expected to be completed in 40 months, and will process an estimated 700,000 barrels of oil per day. Africa's richest man, Aliko Dangote, will lead the project.

events.title: Is US President Donald Trump right to rename AI as 'Super Intelligence'?

events.title: India news: Key opposition leaders meet to discuss poll body row

events.title: Meet 'America': Trump’s AI chatbot changes answers after challenging his claims
events.description: Donald Trump has launched “America”, an AI chatbot designed as a digital portal for US government information. But its responses appear to be changing. The chatbot initially challenged several of Trump’s claims, including on the 2020 election and inflation, providing evidence and links. More recently, it has refused to answer some of the same questions. Other responses still contradict Trump, while some echo his views. Vedika Bahl tests the chatbot, and its varying answers in Truth or Fake.

events.title: UK-France 'one in, one out' migrant exchange deal is scrapped
events.description: A British-French agreement aimed at reducing the number of people trying to cross the English Channel in small boats has been scrapped, London said Wednesday. The pilot programme was intended to break the business model of "people smugglers" by exchanging undocumented migrants who had made the crossing for people who legally applied for asylum.
events.ticker_label: 💥 UK-France 'one in, one out' migrant exchange deal is scrapped

events.title: Syria: An exclusive look at the integration of Uyghur fighters in armed forces
events.description: Several factions of foreign fighters are credited with helping topple Syria's Bashar al-Assad nearly two years ago - among them, the Uyghurs, a predominantly Muslim, Turkic ethnic minority spread across Central Asia - notably in China's Xinjiang region. They eventually became amongst the largest contingents of foreign fighters in Syria, though those who have stayed and built lives there are notoriously secretive. However, France 24's Wassim Nasr was recently in Syria and had exclusive access to Uyghur fighters there.
